original_extraction.evidence_text:
Sometimes Donna would do this on and off for anywhere from a couple of minutes to the better part
of an hour, depending on how powerful her feelings of grief were and how quickly they shifted.
This helped her stay present so she could then choose to focus on a valued activity, instead of
drinking. Sometimes she even added that choice into the commentary: “Now, what do I value doing
at this moment? Well, I was just about to cook something healthy for dinner. Is this something I
value? Yes, it is. So let’s focus on chopping up these potatoes.’

---

Once Donna had chosen a valued activity, she would then connect with it fully, through all of her
five senses. For example, she carefully observed the appearance and texture of the potatoes, the
sounds of peeling and slicing, the feeling of the knife cutting and chopping, and the movements in
her arms, hands and neck.

---

Over time, as her grieving process continued, these feelings and urges troubled her less and less.
And as she got better at expansion, defusion and connection, she needed the thinking self less and
less to assist her.

---

Some people find running commentary extremely helpful; others don’t. So why not give it a go and
see how it works? As always, if it’s helpful, make use of it. And if it isn’t, don’t!

---

We’ll return to connection later in the book, when we use it in taking action. But now it’s time for
something completely different.

---

What do you most dislike about yourself? I've asked this question of hundreds and hundreds of
people, either individually or in groups, and here are some of their most common responses:

---

* I’m too shy/fearful/anxious/needy/fragile/passive/guilty.

---

¢ I’m stupid/silly/disorganised/a time waster.

---

* I’m selfish/critical/arrogant/vain/egotistical/materialistic.

---

¢ I’m judgemental/angry/greedy/aggressive/obnoxious/jealous.

---

* I’m too obsessive/controlling/fastidious/perfectionist.
generation_rules: Use on/off engagement with present-moment awareness depending on intensity and duration of feelings
Focus fully on chosen valued activity through all five senses
pause_rules: Pause or discontinue running commentary if it is not helpful to the individual
original_extraction.psychological_function: Promotes mindfulness and present-moment awareness; supports cognitive defusion from distressing thoughts and feelings; encourages engagement with sensory experience to enhance connection with valued activities.
repetition_rules: Repeat present-moment engagement and defusion practices as needed over time to reduce distress and reliance on thinking self
symbolic_elements: sensory engagement with potatoes (appearance, texture, sound, feeling, movement)
original_extraction.therapeutic_function: Helps individuals stay present and choose valued activities over maladaptive behaviors; facilitates grief processing and reduces distress over time through expansion, defusion, and connection techniques.
voice_rules: Use self-directed questioning to identify valued activities (e.g., 'What do I value doing at this moment?')
Allow flexibility in use of internal commentary based on individual preference
